fullPassage:
A Trip to the Netherlands

Before my trip to the Netherlands, all I knew of the country was that it is famous for windmills and tulips. But as I cycled from place to place, I experienced many things that I hadn't expected, and I wanted to share some of them with you.

"The Anne Frank House and the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam"

My first stop was the Anne Frank House, one of the old buildings lined up along the Prinsengracht, a canal in Amsterdam. Since it was close to the hotel I was staying at, I decided to rent a bike to go there. I enjoyed riding along the canal. The Anne Frank House is one of the most visited museums in the Netherlands. It housed the secret hiding place of Anne Frank.

There was an old bookcase on the second floor. It looked ordinary, but behind it was a secret space where Anne and her family hid for over two years during World War II. The steep stairs and narrow passages gave me a better understanding of what life must have been like for them back then.

After visiting the Anne Frank House, I took a canal cruise on the Prinsengracht. The canal houses I saw along the way had mostly been built during the Dutch Golden Age, which gives them great historical value. Taking the cruise was a great way to see the city from different angles. The gentle touch of the wind made the experience even more pleasant.

"The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam"

Amsterdam is home to a lot of museums, but the Van Gogh Museum was the one I was really excited to visit. The most interesting part of the museum was the way the exhibits were arranged to show how the artist's style had changed over time. The museum showed many of Vincent van Gogh's most well-known works, including my personal favorites: The Bedroom, Sunflowers, and Wheatfield with Crows. The bright colors in The Bedroom seemed to convey a sense of relaxation. The different shades of yellow in Sunflowers were just amazing. In Wheatfield with Crows, the contrast between the bright yellow wheat field and the cool blue sky was striking. Overall, seeing the artworks in person was a very powerful experience.

The museum also displayed the letters that Van Gogh wrote to his younger brother, Theo. Reading those letters, I found out how much the artist loved his brother. After I bought a few postcards with Van Gogh's art on them, I slowly cycled back to the hotel. On my way back, I couldn't help but admire the beautiful, calm, and scenic views of the city, especially people relaxing on the grass and enjoying the sun.

"Windmills in the Zaanse Schans and Seafood in Volendam"

I highly recommend visiting the Zaanse Schans and Volendam if you want to get out of the busy city to experience traditional Dutch culture. A trip to the Netherlands wouldn't be complete without a visit to the windmills. Fortunately, you can get to the Zaanse Schans, which is famous for its windmills, in just 17 minutes by train from Amsterdam.

The moment I saw the village, its beauty took my breath away. Several windmills were spinning by the river in the distance. Soon I felt like I was taken to a point in the past. I looked into one of the working windmills, and it was grinding nuts into oil with its large stone wheels.

Near the windmills, I found a cheese farm and a clog factory. I was surprised by the variety of Dutch cheeses and actually a little unsure about tasting them at first because they were mostly new to me. However, when I tried some of them, they turned out to be incredibly satisfying. I also tried on a few pairs of clogs and found them quite comfortable, which I hadn't expected.

Volendam was a pretty fishing village with neat rows of brick houses with orange roofs. The harbor was dotted with boats. I rented a bike to explore Volendam, and the shop owner said, "In Volendam, do as the locals do and eat seafood." At a restaurant, I ordered one of the Netherlands' most popular dishes, kibbeling. The fried fish snack was hot, fresh, and absolutely delicious!

"The Cube Houses in Rotterdam"

After being completely destroyed during World War II, Rotterdam was restored into a beautiful port city. Experimental and artistic constructions were used to improve the appearance of the city. The Cube Houses in Rotterdam are among the most innovative buildings in the country. The bright yellow houses were something I had been looking forward to seeing, and they were as fantastic as I had expected.

One of the key features of the Cube Houses is that the cubes are tilted by 45 degrees. I visited the Show Cube Museum to get a feel of what life in such a house was like. From the outside, it looked entirely twisted, but once I went inside, it was surprisingly quite comfortable.

For the last few days after the trip, I haven't been able to get the charming sights of the Netherlands out of my mind. If you ever plan to visit the country, I really hope that you will find my post helpful.

Q&A: Are Dutch clogs comfortable?

@Olivia: I wonder if Dutch wooden shoes are comfortable. What do YOU think?

@Liam: I have worn Dutch clogs, and I have to admit they are rather comfortable and useful as well. The wood keeps my feet dry. It easily absorbs sweat and allows the feet to breathe. The wood also provides good support and protects the feet. So they are perfect for activities like gardening, farming, and walking in muddy areas.

@Katie: I tried wearing clogs during a visit to the Netherlands, and I found them uncomfortable. The wood was hard and inflexible, and my feet started to hurt after a while.

@Jacob: After they're worn frequently, or if you wear thick socks, they'll become more comfortable.

@Ashley: I have never worn clogs, but I believe they are probably comfortable for people who are used to them. Clogs have long been a part of Dutch culture, especially in rural regions, and I'd love to try a pair someday.

@Ethan: I purchased a pair of Dutch clogs during my trip to the Netherlands, and I have to say they are not the most comfortable shoes. However, they do look very pretty and unique.

det.korean: 여행 후 며칠간 네덜란드의 매력적인 광경을 잊을 수 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② repulsive: charming(매력적인)의 반의어. 불쾌한, 혐오스러운.
❌ ① attractive(매력적인): 동의어.
❌ ③ delightful(기분 좋은): 동의어.
❌ ④ appealing(매력적인): 동의어.
det.tip: charming(매력적인) ↔ repulsive(불쾌한). attractive, delightful, appealing은 모두 유사어.

questions.passage:
(A) The Anne Frank House is one of the old buildings <u>lined</u> up along the Prinsengracht, a canal in Amsterdam.

(B) I couldn't help but admire the beautiful, calm, and scenic views of the city, especially people relaxing on the grass and enjoying the sun. I waited in <u>line</u> to buy tickets for the next show.
questions.stem: (A)의 'lined'와 (B)의 'line'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 안네 프랑크 하우스는 프린센흐라흐트를 따라 줄지어 있는 오래된 건물 중 하나이다. (B) 다음 공연 표를 사려고 줄을 서서 기다렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) lined up = 줄지어 있다: 건물들이 운하를 따라 늘어서 있음. (B) line = 줄: 표를 사기 위한 대기줄.
❌ ② (A) 선을 긋다: 건물이 선을 긋는 것은 불가. (B) 노선: 맥락 불일치.
❌ ③ (A) 늘어놓다: 가능하나 '줄지어 있다'가 정확. (B) 대사: 공연 표 맥락과 무관.
❌ ④ (A) 안감을 대다: 건물 맥락과 무관. (B) 전화선: 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: line up: 줄지어 있다/줄을 서다. line: 줄, 선, 노선, 대사 등 다의어.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the outer form or look of someone or something"

det.korean: "누군가 또는 무엇의 외적 형태나 모습"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ appearance: 외모, 외관. 정의와 정확히 일치. 본문 'improve the appearance of the city'.
❌ ① construction(건축): 짓는 행위/구조물.
❌ ② atmosphere(분위기): 외형이 아닌 느낌.
❌ ④ experiment(실험): 무관.
det.tip: appearance: 외모, 겉모습. 본문에서 '도시의 외관을 개선하기 위해' 사용됨.

questions.passage: I was surprised by the variety of Dutch cheeses and actually a little unsure about tasting them at first because they were mostly new to me. However, when I tried some of them, they turned out to be incredibly satisfying.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

The __________ (vary) of food options at the market amazed all the visitors.

det.korean: 시장의 음식 선택지의 다양함이 모든 방문객을 놀라게 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ variety: 관사 The 뒤이므로 명사 형태. vary(동사) → variety(명사).
det.tip: vary(동사: 다양하다) → variety(명사: 다양함). various(형용사: 다양한)와 구분.

questions.passage: After being completely destroyed during World War II, Rotterdam was restored into a beautiful port city. Experimental and artistic constructions were used to improve the appearance of the city.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

The scientists conducted an __________ (experiment) study to test the new theory.

det.korean: 과학자들은 새로운 이론을 시험하기 위해 실험적인 연구를 수행했다.
det.analysis: ✅ experimental: 'an __________ study'에서 명사 study를 수식하는 형용사 필요. experiment(명사) → experimental(형용사).
det.tip: experiment(명사: 실험) → experimental(형용사: 실험적인). 'conduct an experimental study' = 실험적 연구를 수행하다.

questions.passage: Near the windmills, I found a cheese farm and a __________. I was surprised by the variety of Dutch cheeses and actually a little unsure about tasting them at first because they were mostly new to me. However, when I tried some of them, they turned out to be incredibly satisfying. I also tried on a few pairs of clogs and found them quite comfortable, which I hadn't expected.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 풍차 근처에서 치즈 농가와 나막신 공장을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① clog factory: 원문 그대로 'a cheese farm and a clog factory'. 뒤에 나막신을 신어본 내용이 이어짐.
❌ ② bicycle shop(자전거 가게): 풍차 마을과 무관.
❌ ③ flower market(꽃 시장): 이 마을에서 언급 없음.
❌ ④ souvenir store(기념품 가게): 원문에 없음.
det.tip: clog: 나막신. 뒤 문장의 'tried on a few pairs of clogs'가 단서.

questions.passage: @Liam: I have worn Dutch clogs, and I have to admit they are rather comfortable and useful as well. The wood keeps my feet dry. It easily absorbs sweat and allows the feet to breathe. The wood also provides good support and protects the feet. So they are perfect for activities like gardening, farming, and __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나막신은 정원 가꾸기, 농사, 그리고 진흙 지역 걷기에 완벽하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ walking in muddy areas: 원문 그대로. 나막신이 발을 건조하게 유지하므로 진흙 지역에 적합.
❌ ① running on a track(트랙 달리기): 나막신과 어울리지 않음.
❌ ② swimming in a pool(수영): 신발과 무관.
❌ ④ climbing a mountain(등산): 나막신으로는 부적합.
det.tip: gardening, farming, walking in muddy areas: 모두 야외/농촌 활동. 나막신의 방수/보호 기능과 연결.
